editions.label: from the workshop
editions.intro: Three Opticell apps have been updated on the App Store, bringing new work to your projects, chats and Chinese studies.

items.body: Project Manager now writes a short Daily Agenda brief with Apple Intelligence, shown at the top of My Day. Your tasks never leave the device for it. A Needs You widget puts your brief and pending handovers on your Home Screen.

MyLLM shows thinking as it arrives from models that reason before answering, folding to a tap-to-read summary. Replies now stream in even when tools are in play, and cloud models keep more of long chats for follow-up questions.

Hanyu adds a Tone Trainer where you hear real words and see your pitch drawn against the target. New Chengyu Idioms covers 48 four-character idioms with story and usage, and new word packs complete HSK 5 and add all of HSK 6.

principles.free: Every Opticell app is free to download. You can install our software and test it on your own device without providing any card details or committing to a purchase. This allows you to judge the utility of the tool before deciding to unlock its full features.
principles.upgrades: You can choose between an ultra-affordable subscription or a one-time lifetime unlock. Both options are entirely opt-in. Subscriptions can be managed or cancelled at any time through your Apple or Google account settings.
principles.pricing: We believe you should know the cost before you commit. Every price is clearly visible on the App Store and Google Play product pages before installation. We also show all costs within the app itself, with no hidden fees or fine print.
principles.privacy: Privacy is our default setting. We do not use analytics to track your usage, nor do we sell information to advertisers or data brokers. Your data stays on your device where it belongs.
principles.ads: Our apps contain no banners, interstitials, or sponsored content. Advertisements compete for your attention and create an incentive for apps to harvest user data. We avoid this model entirely to keep our software focused and clean.
principles.partnership: Where our apps use AI, the technology is designed to extend human capability rather than replace human judgement. The software acts as a tool to assist your workflow, ensuring that you always remain in control of the final outcome.
principles.audience: Our catalogue provides tools for both personal use and professional environments on the same terms. Whether you are using DrawPad for creative work or My Business Portal for organisation, you receive the same honest service.

items.body: MyLLM now shows a thinking model's reasoning as it arrives, folding to one line when the answer begins. Replies from your server or a cloud model appear word by word, and long chats keep more of their history.

Project Manager lets you copy any comment with a press, then pick just the words you need. You can ask two assistants at once and see who is still silent, hand work to Claude on your Mac, and an emoji now counts as picking up a request.

Hanyu adds Tone Trainer for hearing and matching tone patterns, plus a grid that brings back the ones you miss. It gains 48 idioms with story and audio, and HSK 5 and HSK 6 are now complete with twelve new word packs.

editions.label: from the workshop
editions.intro: Three of our apps have had small, useful updates since the last time we wrote about them.

items.body: Project Manager now lets you answer an assistant's proposal straight from the notification, with a reason if you want. A drafted Mail reply can open the original message so your answer stays in the same thread.

MyLLM can now work on code. Open a folder and ask for a fix or feature; it finds the right files, reads them and saves the change with a diff. You can undo or keep each edit. Add an AGENTS.md file to give it your project's rules.

Hanyu adds a Tone Trainer where you hear two-syllable words and see your own pitch drawn against the target. It also brings HSK 6 into the Pack Library and adds forty-eight idioms with their story and how to use them.

editions.label: from the workshop
editions.intro: Three of our apps have had fresh updates on the App Store. Here is what each one now does.

items.body: Project Manager 5.6.1 lets you Apply or Decline a proposed change straight from the notification, with an optional reason. Assistants can also download documents from WorkFlow, and tasks they create no longer default to today.

MyLLM 6.3 adds Work on Code: open a folder of code, ask for a fix or feature, and the assistant finds the files, reads them and saves each change with a diff you can undo. Add an AGENTS.md file to give it your project rules.

Hanyu 3.4 brings Tone Trainer, Chengyu idioms with stories and audio, and HSK 5 and HSK 6 word packs. Hear two-syllable words, match their tone pattern, then say a word and see your pitch drawn against the target.
